definitions.gloss: neologism; newly coined word; new coinage
definitions.explanation: A word that has been recently created or invented, either by combining existing elements in a new way or by introducing an entirely new term. Used in linguistic and media discussions about language evolution.

examples.japanese: この{言葉|ことば}は{最近|さいきん}の{新造語|しんぞうご}だ。
examples.english: This word is a recent neologism.

examples.japanese: SNSの{普及|ふきゅう}で{新造語|しんぞうご}が{次々|つぎつぎ}と{生|う}まれている。
examples.english: With the spread of social media, new coinages are being born one after another.

examples.japanese: {辞書|じしょ}の{編集者|へんしゅうしゃ}は{毎年|まいとし}{新造語|しんぞうご}を{調査|ちょうさ}して、{掲載|けいさい}するかどうかを{判断|はんだん}する。
examples.english: Dictionary editors survey neologisms every year and decide whether to include them.

notes:
Composed of {新造|しんぞう} (newly made) and {語|ご} (word). Japanese has a rich tradition of word creation, particularly through combining kanji compounds, borrowing from English (wasei-eigo), and blending elements from multiple languages.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新造語|しんぞうご}を{作|つく}る: to coin a new word
- {新造語|しんぞうご}が{定着|ていちゃく}する: for a neologism to become established
- {新造語|しんぞうご}が{生|う}まれる: for a neologism to emerge

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {造語|ぞうご}: coined word — a broader term that includes any artificially created word regardless of when it was coined
- {新語|しんご}: new word — a word that has recently entered the language, whether coined or borrowed
- {流行語|りゅうこうご}: buzzword, trendy expression — a word or phrase that is currently popular, but may not be newly created
